claims.text: In-situ mechanical testing combined with high-resolution digital image correlation and SEM/TEM characterization will reveal dynamic deformation mechanisms in FeNiCrMn HEA.
The proposed method will reveal dislocation movement during deformation.
The proposed method will reveal grain refinement during deformation.
Observed deformation mechanisms will correlate with yield strength, ductility, and strain-hardening metrics.
Mechanical-property studies of FeNiCrMn HEA are limited relative to corrosion studies.
As-cast and annealed FeNiCrMn samples exhibit a typical microstructure suitable for the proposed study.
FeNiCrMn HEA has proven corrosion resistance.
Ambient to moderately elevated temperatures and the proposed strain rates are representative of aerospace, energy, and automotive service conditions.
Dislocation activity in FeNiCrMn can be observed dynamically during deformation using the proposed setup.
Potential grain refinement in FeNiCrMn can be observed dynamically during deformation using the proposed setup.
Digital image correlation provides real-time tracking of deformation.
Digital image correlation allows direct correlation of changes in dislocation density and grain-boundary characteristics with mechanical responses.
The proposed method will reliably quantify the mechanical properties of FeNiCrMn HEA.
The deformation mechanisms found in FeNiCrMn will be consistent with those observed in other HEAs subjected to in-situ testing.
FeNiCrMn HEA will demonstrate strain-rate sensitivity.
FeNiCrMn HEA will demonstrate measurable strain-hardening behavior.
Significant deviations in processing or extreme test environments may produce mechanical responses that are not comparable with those from typical as-cast or annealed samples.

contradictions.description: The intervention describes SEM/TEM characterization as subsequent or post-test, while the mechanism and falsification design imply that microstructural evolution, including dislocation structures and grain morphology, is captured dynamically or simultaneously. Digital image correlation measures surface displacement and strain fields, so the stated post-test microscopy does not itself provide simultaneous real-time microstructural observation.
